name: Lunar regolith
why: Feedstock for oxygen, metals, silicon and construction on the Moon

name: Ilmenite (FeTiO3)
why: Hydrogen-reducible to oxygen, iron and titanium oxide

name: Anorthite (lunar highland feldspar)
why: Calcium-aluminium silicate: lunar source of aluminium and oxygen

name: Martian regolith
why: Contains water ice and construction feedstock but carries toxic perchlorates

name: Silicate asteroid material (S-type)
why: Silicates with free iron-nickel metal grains

name: Basalt
why: Melt-spun into basalt fibre for shielding and composites

name: Fused silica glass
why: Windows, optics, solar-cell cover glass and fibre

name: Sintered / 3D-printed regolith
why: Landing pads, berms and habitat shells from local soil

name: Sulfur concrete
why: Waterless concrete suited to the Moon and Mars

name: Alumina (aluminium oxide)
why: Electrical insulator, ceramic fibre and substrate

name: Nextel alumina-boria-silica ceramic fabric
why: Shatters hypervelocity debris in ISS stuffed Whipple shields

name: Boron carbide
why: Neutron absorber for control rods and shielding

name: Silicon carbide
why: High-voltage power electronics and a pressure-retaining layer of TRISO fuel

name: Yttria-stabilised zirconia
why: Oxide-ion electrolyte of solid-oxide electrolysers (MOXIE used scandia-stabilised zirconia)

name: Ultra-high-temperature ceramics (HfC, ZrB2, TaC)
why: Highest-melting ceramics for nozzles, leading edges and hot structures

name: Silica aerogel
why: Ultralight thermal insulation used on Mars rovers

name: Basalt fibre
why: Locally made fabric tested by NASA as a substitute for Nextel in shields

name: Glass fibre
why: Cheap composite reinforcement and the base of Beta cloth

name: Boron nitride nanotubes
why: Candidate structural radiation shielding; boron absorbs neutrons
